name: Breaking Bread
overview: The practice of breaking bread in Scripture is a profound act instituted by Jesus, who blessed, broke, and gave bread to His disciples as a symbol of His body given for them, commanding them to do this in remembrance of Him (Matthew 26:26; Luke 22:19). This sacred act not only commemorates Christ’s sacrifice but also serves as a means by which believers recognize and fellowship with Him, as seen when He was made known to His followers through breaking bread after His resurrection (Luke 24:30, 35). Furthermore, the early church faithfully devoted themselves to breaking bread together, alongside apostolic teaching, fellowship, and prayer, reflecting the integral role this practice held in their communal and spiritual life (Acts 2:42).
